prompts.prompt: Write a Smithy 2.0 model for a Todo service the frontend team will generate a TypeScript client and an OpenAPI spec from: create, get, update (full replace), delete and list todos. A todo has a title (1-200 chars), optional notes, a priority (low/medium/high), a due date and a completed flag. Put the model under model/ and add a smithy-build.json at the root. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's checklist and quality gate (reverse-DNS namespace, @http on every operation, @readonly/@idempotent, specific @error shapes with @httpError, @paginated list, @required/@length/enum constraints, documentation on public shapes) produce a codegen-ready model. Without it, models often skip pagination, errors, idempotency traits or docs.

floor_checks.text: Model files use IDL v2 with a reverse-DNS namespace and a smithy-build.json exists

rubric.criterion: Operations carry correct HTTP and behaviour traits
rubric.pass: Every operation has @http; Get/List @readonly; Update (PUT) and Delete @idempotent; Create uses POST with an idempotency token or a note
rubric.fail: Several operations lack @http or behaviour traits

rubric.pass: Specific client errors (404 not found, 400 validation, optionally 409/429) with @error and @httpError, attached per operation; List is @paginated with inputToken/outputToken/pageSize and a max page size
rubric.partial: Errors or pagination present but generic (one catch-all error) or not wired to operations

rubric.pass: title @required @length(min:1,max:200); priority is an enum; due date a timestamp; @httpLabel ids @required; /// docs on public shapes
rubric.fail: Strings everywhere, no constraints or docs

rubric.criterion: Model is plausibly valid Smithy and the build file is sensible
rubric.pass: No invalid syntax or nonexistent traits; smithy-build.json lists the model source and an openapi/typescript projection or plugin with the assumption noted
rubric.fail: Invented traits or clearly invalid IDL

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?

prompts.prompt: Turn api.txt into a Smithy model under model/ so we can generate a client and an OpenAPI spec. Write DESIGN-NOTES.md with any decisions you made. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: api.txt has constraints and error cases that the skill says to encode (pattern, range, max page size, @sensitive for PII, enum status, specific errors with correct operations attached). A strong model attaches the 409 only to cancel and notes the newest-first ordering, rather than spraying every error on every operation.

floor_checks.text: Namespace is com.acme.logistics and recipientPhone is present

rubric.pass: @pattern 5-digit zips, @range(min:1,max:70000) weightGrams, pageSize max 50, status enum, recipientPhone @sensitive
rubric.partial: Three or four of the five

rubric.criterion: Errors are mapped to the right operations
rubric.pass: 404 on get/status/delete, 400 on inputs, 409 only on the cancel/delete operation, 429 on all (or service-level)
rubric.partial: All errors present but attached indiscriminately

rubric.criterion: Behaviour traits and docs follow the skill
rubric.pass: PUT status and DELETE @idempotent, GET @readonly, list @paginated; docs on public shapes; newest-first sort documented
rubric.partial: Traits right but docs or sort order missing

rubric.pass: DESIGN-NOTES.md states assumptions (e.g. shipmentId format, timestamps) without inventing endpoints
rubric.fail: Adds operations or fields not in api.txt as if specified

prompts.prompt: A teammate wrote model-draft/inventory.smithy. No clients have been generated from it yet. Review it against Smithy best practices and fix it in place so it is ready for client codegen. List what you changed, most severe first, in model-draft/CHANGES.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate orders the fixes (CRITICAL: namespace, missing @http, no error shapes, @httpLabel members not @required; IMPORTANT: docs, pagination, constraints) and its anti-pattern list covers snake_case and missing @sensitive. A strong answer also reasons about whether renaming members is a wire-breaking change.

floor_checks.text: CHANGES.md exists and the draft has no snake_case members left

rubric.criterion: All planted defects are fixed (KEY: namespace, snake_case, PutItem no @http, GetItem not @readonly, DeleteItem not @idempotent, ListItems not @paginated, no errors, @httpLabel not @required, no docs, supplier key not @sensitive, qty no @range)
CHANGES.md is ordered by the skill's severity tiers
rubric.pass: CRITICAL items (namespace, @http, errors, required labels) listed before IMPORTANT (docs, pagination, constraints) and SUGGESTION
rubric.partial: Severities labelled but not ordered, or tiers differ from the gate

rubric.pass: Notes that camelCase renames change restJson wire names and are safe only because no clients exist (or uses @jsonName)
rubric.fail: Claims renames are always harmless when clients exist

rubric.criterion: Fixes stay within the draft's intent
rubric.pass: No new operations beyond what the draft implies; PutItem given a sensible URI with an explained choice
rubric.fail: Rewrites the service with invented scope
